newsitem.title: USA: Gander Mountain plan becomes effective.
newsitem.headline: Gander Mountain plan becomes effective.

text.p: Gander Mountain Inc said Monday its reorganization plan, approved January 23 by U.S. Bankruptcy Court, became effective Monday.

The plan provided for the sale of Gander Mountain's 12 retail stores and substantially all of its assets to Holiday Companies, a privately held Bloomington, Minn.-based retailer and wholesaler of outdoor and other sporting goods as well as gasoline and food products.

Gander said Holiday is paying a purchase price equal to all secured debt, administrative expenses of the bankruptcy, priority claims, plus $19.5 million. It said $18.5 million will be distributed among unsecured creditors, $500,000 paid pro-rata to Gander Mountain preferred shareholders and $500,000 pro-rata to holders of Gander Mountain common stock.
All preferred and common stock of Gander Mountain is canceled, effective immediately.
In July 1996, Holiday acquired five Gander Mountain retail outlets. All 17 Gander Mountain retail stores acquired by Holiday will continue to be operated as Gander Mountain.
